label: Screen flash (a moving carousel that flashes one screen at a time)
description: A product launch's carousel -- a relay piece. 4-10 product screens (full screenshots) stand in a carousel that NEVER stops moving: shape "ring" (default) is a cylinder of screens seen slightly from above (tilt, default 10 deg; each screen turns up to `turn` deg toward the side it faces, so every screen stays readable and no back ever shows) turning slowly and continuously; in a tall box the ring defaults to axis "x", a wheel whose screens roll up over the top; shape "rail" is a horizontal rail of screens receding to the right (yaw 32 deg) sliding continuously left. Screens are rounded (corner), softly shadowed, on the scene background; the far ones sink slightly into it (depth_fade). Each card is its own flat perspective projection with one shared vanishing point and the depth order is a z-index sort, so screens overlap cleanly and never slice through each other. FLASH: on each cue the screen in the front slot LIFTS out of the carousel and punches up to fill the frame (power3.out over flash_in 0.28 s; flash_fit "full" = exactly the component box, i.e. the whole frame plus the camera bleed, image object-fit cover; or a fraction like 0.86 = the screen fitted inside that fraction of the visible frame, centred, corners kept), optionally with a white pop on arrival (flash_pop), holds (hold, default 0.7 s; its label rises bottom-left), then drops back into its slot in the still-moving carousel (power3.inOut over flash_out 0.35 s). Then the next. The carousel is moving the whole time, and it is paced so the screen due next is EXACTLY in the front slot at its lift moment (default order: 0, 1, 2 ... one slot per flash, so the ring accelerates with an accelerating schedule; an explicit `index` makes the ring turn -- always forward, never backwards -- to bring that screen to the front). SCHEDULE (scene seconds; `at` is the ARRIVAL, the hit to put on the beat): lift = at - flash_in; leave = at + hold; return = leave + flash_out. `flashes` [{index?, at, hold?}] sets it outright; `flash_times` [...] gives arrivals in the default order; otherwise the helper: count (default N) flashes, first arrival at first_at (default: enter none -> enter_at + 0.8 + flash_in; point/fade -> the enter's end + 0.35 + flash_in), hold_k = first_hold x (last_hold/first_hold)^(k/(count-1)), the carousel gap before flash k>=1 (from the last return to its lift) = gap_time x (last_gap_time/gap_time)^((k-1)/(count-2)), arrival_k = return_{k-1} + gap + flash_in. Defaults (6 screens, enter none): arrivals 1.08, 2.96, 4.84, 6.72, 8.60, 10.48; returns +1.05. Published on the root (ms precision): data-flash-times (arrivals), data-lift-times, data-leave-times, data-return-times, data-flash-indexes, data-settle-time (hold: the last return; collapse: the collapse end; full: the last arrival), data-front-slot="cx,cy,w,h" (the front slot's untilted card in fractions of the box), data-flash-box="0.5,0.5,w,h", data-from / data-to. ENTER: "none" (default, the carousel standing and moving at frame 0) | "point" (every screen flies out of `from` [x,y] (fractions of the box, default centre) into its slot, scale 0 -> 1, front first -- the hand-off from a dot or a word: frame 0 is empty) | "fade". END: "hold" (default: the carousel keeps turning to the scene end) | "collapse" (at end_at, default last return + 0.3, every screen shrinks into `to` [x,y] over collapse_duration, back first -- the hand-off to a logo or a dot there) | "full" (the last flash never returns: it stays full-frame to the scene end -- a scene join onto a scene that opens on that screen full-frame). Every style is a pure function of the time (a seek anywhere renders the same frame). Full-frame piece: the full-frame slot is the camera layer, 40 px larger than the frame, so every fraction is of that box. Example: {"screens":[{"src":"/assets/metrics.png","w":1920,"h":1080,"label":"Metrics"},{"src":"/assets/traffic.png","w":1920,"h":1080,"label":"Traffic by channel"},{"src":"/assets/funnels.png","w":1920,"h":1080,"label":"Funnels"},{"src":"/assets/retention.png","w":1920,"h":1080,"label":"Retention"},{"src":"/assets/journeys.png","w":1920,"h":1080,"label":"Journeys"},{"src":"/assets/attribution.png","w":1920,"h":1080,"label":"Attribution"}],"enter":"point","from":[0.5,0.5],"flash_times":[1.5,3.5,5,6,6.75],"end":"collapse","to":[0.5,0.5]}.

screens.label: The screens, in order (4-10; strings or {src, w, h (image pixels, default 1920x1080), label?, focus?: [x, y] 0-1 (object-position when a flash crops it)}). The first screen's aspect sets every card's

labels.label: A caption per screen (e.g. "Metrics", "Traffic by channel"), shown bottom-left while it is flashed; a screen's own label wins

shape.label: ring (a turning cylinder seen slightly from above, default) | rail (a receding rail sliding left)

axis.label: ring: y (turns about the vertical: screens travel sideways, the default in a wide box) | x (a wheel: screens roll up over the top, the default in a tall box)

size.label: Front card width, fraction of the box width (ring default: the largest that fits the swept ring in the frame, ~0.40 at 16:9 with 6 screens; rail 0.36, tall 0.62)

ring_radius.label: ring: radius in card widths (axis x: card heights); default max(1, N x 1.14 / 2 pi) (axis x: 1.32)

tilt.label: Degrees the camera looks down on the ring / rail (a wheel: from the side); default 10 (wheel 8)

turn.label: ring: how far a side screen turns to face its side (deg, default 40)

yaw.label: rail: how steeply it recedes to the right (deg, default 32)

front_x.label: rail: the front slot's centre, fraction of the box width (default 0.4; tall 0.5)

gap.label: rail: minimum gap between screens, fraction of a card width (default 0.08); the rail repeats the screens to span the frame

x.label: Shift the ring sideways, fraction of the box width (default 0)

y.label: Shift the ring / rail down, fraction of the box height (default 0)

perspective.label: Camera distance, in multiples of the box's longer side (default 1.9; rail 1.4); smaller = stronger perspective

corner.label: Corner radius, fraction of the card width (default 0.018); a 'full' flash squares off to 0

depth_fade.label: How far the back screens sink into the background colour (0-1, default 0.28)

fog_color.label: The colour they sink into (default: the scene background)

flash_fit.label: full (the flashed screen becomes exactly the component box: the frame) | a fraction, as a number or a string (e.g. 0.86: fitted inside that fraction of the visible frame, centred). Default full; in a tall box with landscape screens 0.92

flashes.label: Explicit flashes [{index?: screen 0-based (default: the next in order), at: ARRIVAL seconds, hold?: seconds}] -- overrides flash_times and the helper

flash_times.label: Arrival moments (s) in the default order (start_index, +stride each)

count.label: Helper: how many flashes (default N, one per screen)

last_hold.label: Helper: the last hold (s, default first_hold); geometric between

gap_time.label: Helper: carousel-only seconds between a return and the next lift (default 0.55)

last_gap_time.label: Helper: the last gap (default gap_time); geometric between (an accelerating cut: e.g. 0.55 -> 0.15)

flash_in.label: Seconds of the lift punch (default 0.28, power3.out)

flash_pop.label: A white pop on the screen as it lands (0.7 peak, gone in 0.24 s); default false (relay bans brightness tricks unless asked)

start_index.label: The screen flashed first in the default order (default 0)

stride.label: Slots the carousel advances per flash in the default order (default 1)

speed.label: Carousel speed before the first and after the last flash, slots per second (default: stride / the mean flash period; 0.25 with fewer than 2 flashes)

enter.label: none (standing at frame 0) | point (every screen flies out of `from`) | fade

enter_duration.label: Seconds each screen takes to enter (point 0.8, fade 0.6)

enter_stagger.label: Seconds spread across the screens, front first (point 0.18, fade 0.12)

from.label: enter point: where the screens come from [x, y], fractions of the box (default [0.5, 0.5]) -- the previous piece's dot

end.label: hold (keeps turning) | collapse (all into `to`) | full (the last flash stays full-frame to the scene end)

end_at.label: collapse: when it starts (default last return + 0.3)

collapse_stagger.label: collapse: seconds spread across the screens, back first (default 0.12)

to.label: collapse: the point [x, y], fractions of the box (default [0.5, 0.5]) -- where the next piece's dot or logo appears

label_size.label: Caption font size, fraction of the box width (default 34 px at 1080p)

label_stays.label: end full: keep the last caption up to the scene end (default false: it drops before the hold ends, so the join frame is the plain screen)
